THE SCIENCE OF THE SIGNAL

Sound, shaped by science.

Vibrasound is an evidence-informed frequency generator. It brings together precise sound, rhythmic movement and color through clear, inspectable mathematical models.

Two tones, one rhythm. Binaural audio sends a slightly different tone to each ear. At 528 Hz with a 6 Hz rhythm, your left ear receives 525 Hz and your right receives 531 Hz. Use stereo headphones.

A rhythm you can hear. Isochronic audio gently raises and lowers the volume at your chosen rate. Volume modulation adds the same pulses to binaural audio when enabled. Pure tone keeps the sound clean; Ethereal adds a musical harmonic bed and space. Chants tunes the timbre of seven recorded vocal sounds to your selected frequency. Turn off “Tune to base frequency” to hear the processed original recording at its natural pitch, with volume pulses at your selected rhythm. MMM and the vowels are sustained; VAM repeats its recorded opening, vowel and nasal closure.

A rhythm you can see. Liquid waves keeps a three-dimensional surface with one source for each audio channel. Actual channel levels shape the waves, and the left/right frequency ratio shapes their relative spacing. The visible animation follows your selected rhythm when sync is enabled; it does not flash at the audible carrier frequency. Shooting stars creates one new meteor per rhythm cycle, so 6 Hz produces six stars per second.

Keep listening. Audio keeps playing when you switch tabs. The session clock continues with it.

Two ways to explore. Science Mode uses explicit acoustic settings and octave-derived colors. Mystic Mode adds symbolic chakra presets, the contemporary Solfeggio system and notes in just intonation. Chakra colors belong to that symbolic palette; they do not replace the octave calculation in Science Mode.

Color through octaves. Your base tone is doubled into the visible spectrum. 528 Hz becomes approximately 516.4 nm: green. The screen represents that wavelength as an RGB color.

Research and signal verification

Rhythmic sound and visual motion are studied through recorded brain responses. Frequency settings here describe the generated stimulus; the application does not measure brain activity. Individual responses depend on the person and the stimulus.

Our audio tests compare rendered samples against the equations, check stereo separation and verify timing in seconds. The display follows within its measured refresh limits.
